# OpenAPI & Swagger Specification Guide

**Project:** MUXARO  
**API Spec Version:** `2.0.0` (dynamically generated by `@fastify/swagger` in `apps/api/src/app.ts`)  
**Interactive UI:** `GET /docs` (`@fastify/swagger-ui`)  
**Machine-Readable JSON:** `GET /docs/json`  
**Machine-Readable YAML:** `GET /docs/yaml`

---

## 1. Accessing Live OpenAPI Documentation

When `apps/api` is running (default `http://localhost:4000`), Fastify automatically generates the OpenAPI 3.x specification directly from registered route schemas across all 13 route plugins under `/api/v1`:

```bash
# Start API server locally
cd apps/api && npm run dev

# Open interactive Swagger UI in browser
# http://localhost:4000/docs

# Fetch live OpenAPI JSON schema
curl -s http://localhost:4000/docs/json | head -n 40
```

> **Note on Legacy Reference Spec:** A historical v1 baseline specification is preserved at `docs/architecture/openapi.yaml` (covering the original media/job/playlist/account routes). The live runtime server (`@fastify/swagger` v2.0.0) and [API Reference](./API_REFERENCE.md) document all **69 implemented `/api/v1` endpoints**, including the full Account Platform, Google OAuth PKCE, TOTP Admin MFA, Rewarded Ads SSV, Tracked Batches, Resumable Multipart Uploads, and Admin Control Centre.

## 2. OpenAPI Metadata & Security Schemes

- **Title:** `MUXARO Media Processing & Account Platform API`
- **Version:** `2.0.0`
- **Base Server (Local):** `http://localhost:4000/api/v1`
- **Production Base URL:** Configured via `API_BASE_URL` / `BASE_URL` (e.g., `https://api.muxaro.app/api/v1`)

### Authentication & CSRF Mechanisms

| Scheme | Transport | Usage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Session Cookie** | `Cookie: muxaro_session=<token>` | Primary browser authentication (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, 30-day TTL) |
| **CSRF Header + Cookie** | `x-muxaro-csrf: <token>` + `Cookie: muxaro_csrf=<token>` | Mandatory on all mutating (`POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`) cookie-authenticated requests |
| **Bearer Token** | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` | Programmatic API / CLI clients (validates against `user_sessions` SHA-256 hash; exempt from browser CSRF) |
| **Guest Session Cookie** | `Cookie: muxaro_guest=guest_<hex>` | Auto-assigned `HttpOnly` cookie isolating unauthenticated visitors |
| **Signed Download Token** | Path param `/api/v1/download/:token` | Time-limited HMAC-SHA256 signed token (`payloadB64.sigB64`) |
| **GAM SSV Signature** | Query/Body `signature` + `key_id` | ECDSA-SHA256 signature verified against Google Ad Manager verifier keys |

## 4. Standard OpenAPI Envelopes (YAML Reference)

```yaml
components:
  schemas:
    ApiSuccessEnvelope:
      type: object
      required: [success, data, requestId]
      properties:
        success:
          type: boolean
          enum: [true]
        data:
          description: Endpoint-specific payload
        requestId:
          type: string
          example: req_a1b2c3d4e5f67890
    ApiErrorEnvelope:
      type: object
      required: [success, error, requestId]
      properties:
        success:
          type: boolean
          enum: [false]
        error:
          type: object
          required: [code, message]
          properties:
            code:
              type: string
              example: ERR_QUOTA_EXCEEDED
            message:
              type: string
            userMessage:
              type: string
            details:
              type: object
              nullable: true
        requestId:
          type: string
```

For full request/response payloads, auth guards, rate limits, and `curl` examples for every endpoint, see [API Reference](./API_REFERENCE.md) and [Error Codes](./ERROR_CODES.md).
